name: Qwen3-Coder-480B-A35B-Instruct
definition: Qwen3-Coder-480B-A35B-Instruct is a large agentic coding Mixture-of-Experts model developed by Qwen / Alibaba in the Qwen3-Coder family. It has 480B parameters with 35B/token active parameters, supports 256K tokens of context, accepts Text / code and produces Text / code. Its primary role is software engineering, repository-scale coding, tool use and coding agents.

key_topics: software engineering, repository-scale coding, tool use and coding agents

details: 160 experts with 8 selected experts per token
~35B active parameters from a 480B total pool
Optimized for agentic coding and tool interaction

training.summary: Qwen3-Coder extends the Qwen3 family toward software engineering and long-horizon coding agents. Its post-training focuses on code generation, repository interaction and tool-oriented behavior rather than generic chat alone.

license.special_conditions: Includes an express patent grant. Model-specific acceptable-use policies, if separately published, are not automatically part of Apache 2.0.
license.legal_note: OpenWeightModels summary for technical comparison; not legal advice.

deployments.notes: Official model page documents vLLM serving.
Direct checkpoint use for compatible workflows.
Publisher FP8 checkpoint available for reduced weight memory.

hardware.summary: 480B total parameters make this a large multi-GPU model even though only 35B are active per token. Tensor/expert parallelism and FP8/other reduced precision are central to production deployment.

limitations: Coding-agent quality depends on the scaffold, tools and repository context—not just the base model.
A 256K model context can be expensive to populate and serve.
MoE routing support and parallelism strategy materially affect throughput.
Autonomous code execution requires separate sandboxing and security controls.
